skills-frq-s1.html:
Part C (1 point). Explain one reason why many people in rural Country A move to its capital city.

Student answer: "Jobs."

skills-frq-s2.title: A second practice part and answer (written for practice, LevlPrep 2026)
skills-frq-s2.html:
Part G (1 point). Explain the degree to which data for each province of Country A are more useful than one national figure for deciding where to build new clinics.

Student answer: "Province data show which provinces have the fewest clinics, so the government can build where the need is greatest."

items.q: Read the legend of this map. What do the shades measure?
options: The total number of people in each country
How many people live in each square kilometer
How fast each country's population is growing
The share of each country's people who live in cities

items.q: Which statement describes the pattern on this map, naming places?
options: Bangladesh is in the top class and India in the second class
India is in the top class (1 billion or more) and Bhutan in the lowest (under 10 million)
Afghanistan and Nepal are in the darkest class, and India is in the lightest class
Sri Lanka and Pakistan are both in the lowest class

items.q: A student looks at this map and writes: "India is the most crowded country in South Asia, because it is the darkest." What is wrong with the claim?
options: The map has no source line, so a reader has no way to check where its numbers came from
Dark shades on this map stand for the lowest values, so India has the fewest people shown
It reads a totals map as a crowding map; Bangladesh fits more people on each square kilometer
India is shaded in the lightest class, so the student read the colors in reverse

items.q: What trend does the chart show for River Town?
options: It shrank in each decade, from about 50,000 people in 1990 to about 20,000 in 2020
It stayed at about 30,000 people from 1990 to 2020, with little change
It grew until 2000 and then shrank in each decade after that
It grew each decade, from about 20,000 people in 1990 to about 50,000 in 2020

items.q: In which year did the two towns have about the same number of people?
Which statement can you support with this chart, and which needs other data?
options: Supported: people moved from Hill Town to River Town. Needs other data: the years
Supported: Hill Town lost people from 1990 to 2020. Needs other data: why people left
Supported: River Town has more jobs. Needs other data: the number of people
Supported: both towns grew over the 30 years. Needs other data: the units on the axis

items.q: Which source line is complete enough to trust for a class report?
options: From the internet, found by searching for the topic
A website about countries, with facts about each one
UN World Population Prospects 2024, 2024 estimates
Government numbers, recent, from the population office

items.q: In an invented town of 40,000 people, 10,000 people ride a bus each day. What percent of the town's people ride a bus each day?

mistakes.why: You divided the whole by the part. A share is the part (riders) divided by the whole (all the people), times 100.

items.q: A table lists "Hospital beds per 1,000 people": Town P has 4 and Town Q has 2. Which statement does the table support?
options: Town P has more hospital beds in total than Town Q
Town Q has more people than Town P
Town Q has 2 hospital beds, half as many as Town P has
Town P has more beds for each 1,000 people than Town Q

items.q: Put the four steps for reading a map, table or chart in order.
options: Read the title: what, where and when
Read the legend and the units
Read the source line: who and what year
Describe the pattern, naming places and values

items.q: What is the scale of analysis of the data on this map?
options: Local (subnational): one value for each province
National: the map shows the whole of one country
Global: the data could be compared with other countries
Regional: Country A counts as a region of the world

items.q: The title gives one national figure: 60% of homes have internet access. What does the map show that the national figure hides?
options: Access is about 60% in each province, just as the national figure says
Access is 80% or more in the Capital Region but under 40% in the Western Uplands
Country A has more homes with internet than its neighbors have
Access is rising faster in the Western Uplands than it is in the Capital Region these days

items.q: Country A's government can build new internet lines in two provinces this year. Which data should it use to choose them, and why?
options: The national figure of 60%, because one number is easier to compare with other countries
A world map of internet access, because it covers the most land and the most countries
The province data, because they show access is lowest in the Western Uplands and Southern Forest
The province data, because the Capital Region has the highest access of any province

items.q: A world map is shaded so that each country has one color for its share of people living in cities. What is the scale of analysis of its data?
options: Global: the map shows the whole world
Local: cities are measured
Regional: the countries are grouped into world regions
National: there is one value for each country

items.q: On a map with a scale of 1:50,000, two villages are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they on the ground, in kilometers?

mistakes.why: That is the distance in centimeters (4 x 50,000). Divide by 100,000 to turn centimeters into kilometers.
A factor of 10 off: 100,000 cm make 1 km, so 200,000 cm is 2 km, not 20 km.

items.q: Which map is the large-scale map?
options: A map of one neighborhood at 1:5,000
A map of the world at 1:100,000,000
A map of a continent at 1:20,000,000
A map of a large country at 1:10,000,000

items.q: Put the four scales of analysis in order, from the largest area to the smallest.
options: Global scale
Regional scale
National scale
Local scale

items.q: A student writes: "A large-scale map shows a large area, like the whole world." Which correction is right?
options: A large-scale map shows a medium area, such as one country, with average detail
A large-scale map shows a small area, such as a town, in great detail
A large-scale map covers more ground than a small-scale map does
A large-scale map shows data at the global scale of analysis, not the local

items.q: Build a sentence that names the scale of analysis of the Country A internet map and what it shows.

specific.frame: At the ___ scale, the data show that ___.
specific.model: At the local (subnational) scale, the data show that internet access is 80% or more in the Capital Region but under 40% in the Western Uplands of Country A.

scale.label: Scale of analysis
options: local (subnational)
national
global

why.1: The map shows one country, but each value is for a province: that is local (subnational) data.
why.2: Global data would give values for many countries; these are provinces of one country.

pattern.label: Pattern with places
options: access is highest in the Capital Region and lowest in the Western Uplands
access varies
access is 60% across Country A

why.1: Too vague to earn credit: say where it is high and where it is low.
why.2: 60% is the national average; the map shows provinces far above and below it.

items.q: Egypt's national figure for people per square kilometer is moderate, yet almost all Egyptians live in the Nile valley and delta. What does this show about scale?
options: National data for Egypt are wrong, so the national figure should be thrown out
Egypt's people are spread evenly across the valley, the delta and the desert
A pattern can change with scale: the national figure hides a crowded valley and an empty desert
The national figure is more accurate than local data, so it settles the question

items.q: Would this answer earn the point for Part C?
options: No: it names a reason but does not say how jobs in the capital lead people to move
Yes: "jobs" is a correct reason, and a correct reason earns the point whatever the verb asks
No: the answer needs a number from a data source
Yes: short answers are scored higher because they are clear

items.q: Which rewrite of the student's answer would earn the point?
options: "Jobs are a very important reason why people move to the capital city of Country A."
"The capital has more paid jobs than rural areas, so people move there to earn higher wages."
"There are jobs in the capital city of Country A, and there are also schools and hospitals there."
"Rural people in Country A move to the capital city, which is a large and busy city."

items.q: Which task verb would the student's one-word answer, "Jobs", fully satisfy?
options: Explain
Describe
Identify
Compare

items.q: What does this answer still need to earn the point?
options: A second province named, to give the answer more places
A definition of a clinic, so the reader knows the term
A comparison with another country that has more clinics
A stated degree at the start, such as "To a high degree"

items.q: The answer says province data are more useful. At what scale of analysis are province data?
options: Local (subnational)
National (one value for the country)
Regional (a group of countries)
Global (the whole world)

items.q: Which opening would make the answer fully match its verb?
options: "Province data are data for each province, which is part of a country..."
"To a high degree: province data show which provinces have the fewest clinics, so..."
"Clinics are places where people get health care, such as doctors..."
"National data and province data are two kinds of data that..."

items.q: Which task verb asks you to speak about both of two things?
options: Describe
Identify
Compare
Define

items.q: A part asks: "Describe the pattern of farming shown on the map." Which answer earns the point?
options: "The farms are spread out in some places and close together in others on this map."
"Farming is important to Country A because many people there work on farms and sell crops in nearby towns."
"Farms are found in Country A, as the map shows."
"Most farms are along the river in the south of Country A, and few are in the dry hills of the north."

items.q: Build an explain answer that would earn a point: why might a new highway change where people in a city shop?

specific.model: In Country A's capital, the new highway cuts the driving time to stores on the edge of the city, so more people shop there instead of downtown.

place.label: Place
options: Country A's capital
some cities

why.1: Too vague: name the place the answer is about.

cause.label: Cause
options: cuts the driving time to stores on the edge of the city
is a large road

why.1: That describes the highway but gives no cause that would change shopping.

effect.label: Effect
options: more people shop there instead of downtown
the highway is busy

why.1: That is not about where people shop, which is what the question asks.

items.q: Each free-response question on the AP® Human Geography exam has parts A to G. How are the parts scored?
options: Each part is worth 1 point, judged against one rubric line
Each part is worth up to 3 points for longer answers
The whole question is scored once, for overall quality
Points go to answers that use the most key terms
